I still make mistakes. I make them faster now.
The models will analyse wider, deeper and faster. What will your insight be?

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 line 11 (expanded): "This is where \"building got cheap, deciding didn't\" stops being an edge" - quoted thesis phrase names itself, is the training's own spine claim (also in apt101-building-is-cheap.md, earlier in module arc), and the quote above supplies the 'rivals' frame; chunk 3 'your rivals' models' resolves to chunk 1 header. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.

No positional pointer to another file in any chunk; closest: chunk 3 'your rivals' models too' points back inside the same file (sequential callback, allowed). grep for 'lecture|earlier|opening' in body slides: none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 1 'what would change this training's mind' - forward-looking, not an event they did; 'building got cheap, deciding didn't' is the training's thesis phrase that exists in apt101-building-is-cheap.md. No 'the X you did/saw' reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no live-demo or guess-before-reveal beat in any chunk

rules_evaluated.evidence: Each chunk carries a self-standing claim: chunk 2 line 24 'your team's next wrong bet can show itself in days'; chunk 3 line 33 'models ... are your rivals' models too'. Closest to thin: chunk 3 (two sentences) but it holds a claim and an ask.

Closest: chunk 3 header is a question; body line 33 answers the premise (models shared) and hands the question over, so header does not contradict content. Chunk 1 header 'Cheap building helps your rivals too' matches line 11 'When rivals build as cheaply, speed is the entry price'.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.', no triples, no superlatives, no number+retraction, no abstraction stacks, no verb triplets. Closest: chunk 1 line 13 'choosing the outcome and reading a no as clearly as a yes' - a pair, concrete.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings should be claims: chunk 1 'Cheap building helps your rivals too' (claim), chunk 2 quote claim. Closest: chunk 3 header is a question (line 28 'What will your insight be?'). Rule binds law/consolidation slides; this closer deliberately hands the open question over and the header carries the squint title, so a claim header would waste the question. Within the rule's orientation/closer allowance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.

Chunk 2 line 24 adds a consequence (days, time to place a better bet) beyond the quote.
